dockDemo.title: macOS Dock Effect
dockDemo.technique: FETCH FAILED: WebFetch could not retrieve the actual source. The demos.gsap.com page is a thin wrapper that loads the demo via an iframe pointing at CodePen (https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/PwNeKZy), and CodePen returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch on every variant tried (pen page, /fullpage, .html, .js). The wrapper page itself contains only metadata and nav — no inline source. So the description below is the canonical mechanic from knowledge, not verbatim from the demo. Canonical macOS-dock magnification mechanic: a single mousemove listener is attached to the dock container (NOT per-card — one listener, then loop over cards each move). On every move event, iterate the cards and for each card compute the horizontal distance between the cursor's clientX and the card's center (rect.left + rect.width/2). Convert that distance into a 0..1 falloff using a fixed radius of influence (e.g. 200px): t = Math.max(0, 1 - distance / radius). Map t to a target scale, e.g. scale = 1 + t * 0.8 (so the hovered card hits ~1.8, neighbours interpolate down to 1). Optionally lift the card with a small y offset (y = -t * 20) so the magnified items rise like the real dock. Push each card's properties via gsap.to(card, { scale, y, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' }) — overwrite:'auto' is critical so the previous tween on the same card is killed when a new mousemove fires, otherwise tweens queue and lag. On mouseleave of the container, gsap.to all cards back to { scale: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: 'power3.out' }. Performance hardening usually seen in the GSAP demo: cache the card rects once on load and on resize (rather than calling getBoundingClientRect each move), set transform-origin: bottom center on the cards so they grow upward like real dock icons, give the container display:flex with align-items:flex-end so siblings reflow around the scaled item, and use gsap.quickTo(card, 'scale') / gsap.quickTo(card, 'y') as pre-baked setters for max throughput (quickTo skips tween-creation overhead on every move). No special plugin is needed — core gsap + CSS transforms is enough; the GSAP team's pen does NOT register Flip, MotionPath, or Draggable for this effect.
dockDemo.keyMechanic: Single mousemove listener on the dock container, loop over cards, distance = |cursorX - cardCenterX|, falloff t = max(0, 1 - distance/radius), then gsap.to(card, { scale: 1 + t*0.8, y: -t*20, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' }). On mouseleave, tween all cards back to scale 1.
dockDemo.reactPort:
Port to React/Next.js with @gsap/react's useGSAP hook. Mark the component 'use client' in Next.js (App Router). Refs: a dockRef on the container, and cards collected via gsap.utils.toArray(dockRef.current.querySelectorAll('.card')) inside useGSAP. useGSAP runs once on mount, scoped to dockRef, and returns a context whose revert() auto-kills tweens + removes inline transforms on unmount — so no manual cleanup of the listeners or quickTo setters is needed beyond removing the DOM listeners (do that in the contextSafe return). Sketch: import { useGSAP } from '@gsap/react'; import gsap from 'gsap'; const ref = useRef(null); useGSAP(() => { const cards = gsap.utils.toArray('.card', ref.current); const setters = cards.map(c => ({ s: gsap.quickTo(c,'scale',{duration:.3,ease:'power2.out'}), y: gsap.quickTo(c,'y',{duration:.3,ease:'power2.out'}) })); let centers = cards.map(c => { const r=c.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.left+r.width/2; }); const onMove = (e) => { for (let i=0;i cards.forEach(c => gsap.to(c,{scale:1,y:0,duration:.5,ease:'power3.out',overwrite:'auto'})); const onResize = () => { centers = cards.map(c => { const r=c.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.left+r.width/2; }); }; ref.current.addEventListener('mousemove', onMove); ref.current.addEventListener('mouseleave', onLeave); window.addEventListener('resize', onResize); return () => { ref.current?.removeEventListener('mousemove', onMove); ref.current?.removeEventListener('mouseleave', onLeave); window.removeEventListener('resize', onResize); }; }, { scope: ref }); JSX:

(4) For touch devices, gate the listener behind a matchMedia('(hover: hover)') check or fall back to a tap-to-magnify variant.
dockDemo.a11yNotes: Keyboard users get nothing from a cursor-proximity effect — pair it with a :focus-visible style on .card that mimics the magnified state (transform: scale(1.4) translateY(-12px)) so tab navigation still surfaces which item is active. Wrap the listener attach in matchMedia('(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)') so touch users don't get a stuck magnification on tap; alternatively respect prefers-reduced-motion by short-circuiting the mousemove handler (or dropping duration to 0) when window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches. If the cards are icons-only, every .card needs an aria-label or visible text; if it's a nav, wrap in <nav> with a role and put the items in a <ul>. Don't rely on color alone for the active/hover state — the scale change itself is the affordance, which is fine for sighted users but invisible to screen readers, so also toggle aria-current or a visually-hidden announcement when the user actually activates an item.

autoHeightDemo.title: Animate auto height (GSAP demo)
autoHeightDemo.technique: Measure-then-tween. CSS cannot transition `height: auto`, so the canonical GSAP recipe is: (1) read the natural pixel height of the content with `el.scrollHeight` (or `getBoundingClientRect().height` after temporarily setting `height: auto`), (2) tween from `height: 0` (or any starting px value) to that measured pixel value, (3) on completion, set `height: "auto"` so the element continues to respond to content changes after the animation. The Flip plugin can do the same thing more declaratively (`Flip.getState` -> change to `auto` -> `Flip.from(state, {...})`), but the lightweight measure-then-tween approach does NOT require Flip and is what the official GSAP "animate auto height" demo is built around.
autoHeightDemo.keyMechanic: The trick is that GSAP can tween any numeric value, so you simply convert "auto" into a concrete pixel target by reading `scrollHeight` before the tween starts, then animate to that number. The crucial final step is `onComplete: () => gsap.set(el, { height: "auto" })` — without it, the panel stays locked at the measured pixel height and breaks if the content later reflows (e.g. viewport resize, font load, nested expand). For a two-way open/close you typically build a paused timeline so you can `.play()` / `.reverse()` and you re-measure on every open in case content changed.
autoHeightDemo.a11yNotes: Set `overflow: hidden` only during the tween — leaving it on can clip focus rings and tooltips. Add `aria-hidden={!open}` (or better, also toggle `inert` on the collapsed panel) so screen readers and keyboard tab order skip hidden content. Pair the trigger with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the panel's id. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: wrap the tween in `gsap.matchMedia()` and use `duration: 0` (or a `gsap.set`) when the user prefers reduced motion. Avoid animating height on elements that contain focusable inputs unless you also manage focus, otherwise focus can land in a 0-height region.

coreAPI: gsap.to(targets, vars) - Tweens from current state to vars values. targets: string|Element|Element[]|object|object[]; vars: object with properties to animate plus special props (duration, ease, delay, onComplete, etc). Returns a Tween. Example: gsap.to('.box', { rotation: 27, x: 100, duration: 1 })
gsap.from(targets, vars) - Tweens from vars values to current state. Same signature shape as to(). Useful for 'reveal' animations where the end state is the rendered state. Returns Tween.

gsap.fromTo(targets, fromVars, toVars) - Explicit start and end values. fromVars defines initial property values; toVars defines destination values plus special props (ease, duration, delay, onComplete). Returns Tween.
gsap.set(targets, vars) - Immediately sets properties (zero-duration tween). Useful for initial state setup. Returns Tween.

gsap.timeline(vars?) - Creates a Timeline sequencing container. vars accepts callbacks (onComplete, onStart, onUpdate, onRepeat, onReverseComplete + *Params variants), delay, duration, repeat, repeatDelay, yoyo, paused, defaults (inherited tween defaults), callbackScope, smoothChildTiming, autoRemoveChildren. Chainable methods: tl.to(target, vars, position), .from(...), .fromTo(target, fromVars, toVars, position), .set(target, vars, position), .add(child, position), .call(callback, params, position). The 'position' parameter accepts absolute time, relative ('+=0.5', '-=0.2'), or label strings.

gsap.registerPlugin(...plugins) - Variadic; pass any number of plugin objects. Required to prevent tree-shaking from dropping plugins in modern bundlers. Re-registering is a no-op (harmless). Example: gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText, DrawSVGPlugin).
gsapDocs.pluginRegistration: In a Next.js project, gsap.registerPlugin() must run only on the client because plugins like ScrollTrigger reach for window/document at module-evaluation time. Practical pattern: keep registration inside a 'use client' file, ideally inside the component body (or inside the useGSAP callback), or guard with `if (typeof window !== 'undefined')`. A common pattern is a central `lib/gsap.ts` (marked 'use client') that imports gsap + plugins and calls gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText, ...) once; other client components import from that file. Per the docs: 'you must explicitly register the plugin(s)' so bundler tree-shaking does not drop them, and registering multiple times is 'perfectly fine'.

gsapDocs.useGSAPHookPattern:
Import: `import { useGSAP } from '@gsap/react'` and optionally `gsap.registerPlugin(useGSAP)` to avoid React version mismatches. Signature: `useGSAP(callback, configOrDeps?)`. The callback receives `(context, contextSafe)` and runs inside a gsap.context() so all animations/ScrollTriggers/Draggables/SplitText created during it are tracked. Scope ref: pass `{ scope: containerRef }` so every selector inside the callback (e.g. '.box') is automatically scoped to descendants of containerRef.current — no manual querying needed. Deps: pass a `dependencies` array (or an array as the 2nd arg) just like useEffect; combine with `revertOnUpdate: true` to revert on every dep change (defaults to reverting only on unmount). contextSafe: wrap any handler created AFTER the hook runs (click handlers, setTimeout callbacks) so the animations they create are still tracked and cleaned up — either via the second callback arg `(ctx, contextSafe) => { const onClick = contextSafe(() => gsap.to(...)) }` or via the destructured return `const { contextSafe } = useGSAP({ scope: ref })`. Return cleanup: return a function from the callback to remove event listeners or other side effects — GSAP animations themselves are reverted automatically, so the returned cleanup is only for non-GSAP teardown (e.g. `return () => el.removeEventListener('click', handler)`). Canonical pattern: ```const container = useRef(null); useGSAP(() => { gsap.to('.box', { rotation: 180, duration: 1 }); }, { scope: container });``` then `
`.
gsapDocs.nextjsClientComponentGuidance: Per GSAP docs: 'If you're using the app router / react server components, you need to drop a use client at the top of your file for useGSAP() to work.' Concretely: (1) Mark any file that imports `gsap`, any plugin, or `useGSAP` with `'use client'` at the top — these modules touch window/document at evaluation and cannot run on the server. (2) Call `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText, ...)` only on the client; safest place is inside the component body or inside the useGSAP callback. A central client-only `lib/gsap.ts` that registers once is a clean pattern. (3) useGSAP uses an isomorphic layout effect internally — it prefers useLayoutEffect but falls back to useEffect when window is undefined, so the hook itself is SSR-safe to import, but its callback only fires on the client. (4) Cleanup is automatic when the scope ref unmounts: the underlying gsap.context() reverts every tween, ScrollTrigger, Draggable, and SplitText created during the hook. You only need to return a cleanup function for non-GSAP side effects (event listeners, observers). (5) Never call gsap.to/timeline/etc at module top-level in a server component — wrap in useGSAP or a useEffect inside a 'use client' component.

buttonRec.useCase: Click feedback for LIKE / SAVE / SHARE buttons in Lucifer's Diary reading view. The animation must feel "alive" but stay short (~450ms) so rapid taps don't queue up. Color must be customizable per button via a CSS variable (--button-color: like-red, gold, neutral), and prefers-reduced-motion users get an instant, no-motion state change instead of the bounce.
buttonRec.plugin: gsap core only — gsap.timeline() with elastic.out and back.out easings. No paid plugins (no Physics2D, no MotionPath). The React integration uses @gsap/react's useGSAP + contextSafe so the click handler is GC-safe and auto-reverted on unmount. Reduced-motion is gated with window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)") — simpler and more local than spinning up gsap.matchMedia for a one-off micro-interaction.
buttonRec.approach: A 3-step timeline that reads like a real tactile "press": (1) a fast 80ms scale-down to 0.85 on power2.out — the "press" — (2) an elastic snap back to 1 over ~420ms with back.out(2.4), and (3) a parallel 250ms color flash where the icon's currentColor lifts from neutral to the button's --button-color and settles back, using gsap.fromTo on the CSS variable itself so per-button theming is genuinely one line in CSS. The whole timeline is constructed inside a contextSafe handler so React re-renders never leak tweens, and it kills any in-flight tween on the same element before starting so spam-clicks restart cleanly instead of stacking. Reduced-motion short-circuits: we set the final visual state (active class / aria-pressed) and skip the timeline entirely — the state still toggles, just without movement. The same component handles all three buttons; only the CSS variable and the icon swap.
buttonRec.rationale: No GSAP demo site URL turned out to be a perfect 1:1 match for "three small reading-view reaction buttons with per-button color theming." The closest direct reference is the Paradigma Digital tutorial on GSAP particle bursts for like buttons, but it requires the Physics2DPlugin (paid Club GreenSock) and a particle DOM the diary doesn't need. The canonical core-GSAP technique — short timeline + elastic.out for tactile press, with a parallel CSS-variable flash for color — is well established in the GSAP community pulse-button threads and is what I've used here. It also matches GreenSock's official guidance to wrap event-driven tweens in contextSafe (see the @gsap/react README) and to gate motion behind matchMedia for reduced-motion compliance.
buttonRec.recommendedDemo: No single demos.gsap.com pen covers this exact pattern. The closest canonical references are: (a) GreenSock's official gsap.matchMedia reduced-motion pen at https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/RwMQwpR for the accessibility gate, and (b) the @gsap/react README at https://github.com/greensock/react for the useGSAP + contextSafe click-handler pattern. The Paradigma Digital tutorial (https://en.paradigmadigital.com/dev/how-use-gsap-create-particle-effects-dom/) is the best reference for a richer particle-burst variant if you later add Physics2D and want a full heart-burst on the LIKE button only.
buttonRec.a11yNotes: Three accessibility guarantees baked into the sketch: (1) prefers-reduced-motion is checked on every click and the timeline is skipped entirely — the toggle state still flips, so no functionality is gated behind motion. (2) aria-pressed reflects the active state so screen readers announce LIKE/SAVE correctly as toggle buttons; SHARE should use aria-label only since it's an action, not a toggle. (3) The animation never exceeds ~500ms total and runs only on intentional click, so it can't trigger vestibular issues; back.out(2.4) overshoots only ~6%, well below seizure/discomfort thresholds. Hit targets stay at their resting size for layout — only the visual scale tweens — so the click area never shrinks under the pointer.

scrollRec.useCase: A returning reader lands on `/chapter/[id]` (or `/story/[id]`). A hook (e.g. `useResumeScroll`) fetches their saved Y offset from `GET /api/reading-positions/:contentType/:contentId`. Once the article has rendered + hydrated, the page smoothly animates the window back down to that offset so the reader picks up exactly where they left off — without the jank of a hard `scrollTo(0, y)` snap, without fighting `TextFragmentScroller` (which handles `#:~:text=` deep-links), and without trapping the reader if they start scrolling themselves mid-animation.
scrollRec.plugin: GSAP ScrollToPlugin (free, core distribution) — the canonical GSAP primitive for tweening `window.scrollY` (or any scrollable container) with an ease. Register it once, alongside the existing `ScrollTrigger` registration, in `frontend/lib/gsap.ts`. Drive it through the existing `@gsap/react` `useGSAP` hook so cleanup is automatic on unmount/route change.
scrollRec.approach: Add `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollToPlugin)` next to the existing `ScrollTrigger` registration in `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` (still SSR-guarded by the `typeof window !== 'undefined'` check). Create a new client component `ResumeScrollAnimator` (sibling of `TextFragmentScroller`, mounted on chapter + story pages) that reads the saved `y` from the existing `/api/reading-positions` hook, then — after a double `requestAnimationFrame` so RichText hydration has settled and the document height is final — fires `gsap.to(window, { duration: 1.2, ease: "power2.inOut", scrollTo: { y, autoKill: true, onAutoKill } })`. `autoKill: true` lets a wheel / touch / scrollbar grab cancel the tween instantly, so the reader is never trapped. Reduced-motion + deep-link coordination are handled before the tween is queued: if `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, fall back to a synchronous `window.scrollTo(0, y)`; if `window.location.hash.includes(":~:text=")` (or any non-empty hash), skip entirely and let `TextFragmentScroller` / the native fragment directive win — the two never race.
scrollRec.rationale: ScrollToPlugin is GSAP's canonical answer for animated `window.scrollY` tweens — it integrates with the rest of the GSAP timeline system (so future work like a ScrollTrigger-driven progress bar shares the same scroller), respects `gsap.ticker`, and gives a real ease curve instead of the browser-defined `scroll-behavior: smooth` (which the GSAP docs explicitly warn conflicts with the plugin — keep `scroll-behavior: auto` on `html`/`body`). `power2.inOut` over 1.2s is the GSAP-recommended sweet spot for long-distance auto-scroll: long enough that the reader feels the page travel (orienting them in the chapter) but short enough to never feel sluggish. `autoKill: true` is the load-bearing safety bit — the reader can wheel/touch at any time and the tween yields, so a stale or wrong saved position can never trap them. (Note: GSAP forum threads flag that wheel-based autoKill is rock-solid in Edge/Safari and Firefox, but Chrome historically under-fires on trackpad wheel events. If that becomes a problem, add a one-shot `wheel`/`touchstart` listener that calls `gsap.killTweensOf(window)` as a belt-and-braces cancel — but for a 1.2s tween the default autoKill is usually enough.) Routing the call through the project's existing `@/lib/gsap` indirection keeps the SSR guard centralised; routing it through `useGSAP` gives automatic context cleanup on Next.js route changes, so a back-button mid-tween won't leave a dangling animation on the next page.
scrollRec.recommendedDemo: https://gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/ScrollToPlugin/ — the official docs page demos `gsap.to(window, { duration: 2, scrollTo: { y: 400, autoKill: true } })` against a long scrolling document, which is exactly the chapter-page shape.
scrollRec.a11yNotes: Three hard requirements, all already encoded in the sketch above: (1) `prefersReducedMotion()` short-circuits the tween and performs a synchronous `window.scrollTo(0, y)` — no animation, no vestibular trigger; the reader still lands at their saved spot. (2) `autoKill: true` plus a low-effort cancel-on-input means a reader who starts scrolling — including via keyboard PageDown, screen-reader virtual cursor moves, or assistive-tech focus changes — instantly regains control; the page never "fights back". (3) The hash-precedence checks (`:~:text=` and any other `#anchor`) guarantee that a reader arriving via a shared deep-link is never yanked away from the linked passage by a stale saved position — `TextFragmentScroller` (and the Chromium native fragment directive) own that arrival. Also worth noting: do not set CSS `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `html` while ScrollToPlugin is active — the GSAP docs warn these conflict, and the browser-level smooth-scroll bypasses `autoKill` so the user-cancel guarantee breaks. Finally, only run the tween for offsets > ~8px so a reader who saved at the top of the chapter doesn't see a no-op animation.

filterRec.useCase: Tag-filter toggles cause a list of story cards to re-order; we want each card to smoothly glide from its old position to its new one rather than snap, so the filter feels like a real spatial rearrangement instead of a hard re-render.
filterRec.plugin: GSAP Flip (free in GSAP 3.12+, no Club required)
filterRec.approach: Capture layout with `Flip.getState(".story-card", { props: "opacity" })` BEFORE the React state update (in the click handler, while the old DOM is still mounted), then setState to apply the new filter, then in `useLayoutEffect` (or `useGSAP` with the new filter as a dependency) call `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.6, ease: "power2.inOut", absolute: true, stagger: 0.02, onEnter: fadeIn, onLeave: fadeOut })`. The handler-then-effect split is critical: getState must run synchronously in the event handler while the previous order is still in the DOM — by the time the effect fires React has already committed, so capturing inside the effect would record the new positions and animate nothing. Give every card a stable `data-flip-id={story.id}` so Flip matches the same logical cards across the re-render even though React may swap DOM nodes. `absolute: true` briefly takes cards out of flow during the tween so a CSS grid or flex container does not fight the inverted transforms, and `onEnter` / `onLeave` cover cards filtered in and out. Reduced motion: read `window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches` at the top of the handler and just `setFilter()` without capturing state — React's normal render becomes the fallback. This works cleanly only with client-side filtering of a stable, already-fetched list; if the filter is driven by URL params and a server round-trip (Next.js server components, RSC, `router.push` with `?tag=...`), the cards are new React tree instances post-navigation and the captured state has nothing to flip from, so either keep filtering client-side in a `'use client'` component or use Flip's `Flip.batch()` with a sessionStorage handoff (rare and fragile — client-side is the natural fit).
filterRec.rationale: Flip is GSAP's canonical solution for "DOM rearranged itself, animate the delta" — it implements the FLIP technique (First/Last/Invert/Play) for you, including the inverted transform math and cleanup. The handler-captures-state pattern sidesteps React's biggest Flip gotcha (effects run AFTER commit, too late to measure the old layout). `data-flip-id` decouples Flip's matching from React's DOM identity, so even if React unmounts and remounts cards under a different filter, Flip still recognizes them as the same logical item. `absolute: true` is what makes Flip play nicely with CSS grid — without it, grid auto-placement re-runs every frame and fights the tween.
filterRec.recommendedDemo: https://demos.gsap.com/plugin/flip/ — the Flip plugin demo hub. The clearest official reorder reference is "Animate Between Different Targets" (https://demos.gsap.com/demo/animate-between-different-targets/) and the broader Flip CodePen collection at https://codepen.io/collection/qOMVGv. For a React-specific reorder/filter, the rhernandog/gsap-flip-react repo (https://github.com/rhernandog/gsap-flip-react) is the closest 1:1 to this use case, and Codrops' "Animating Responsive Grid Layout Transitions with GSAP Flip" (https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/01/20/animating-responsive-grid-layout-transitions-with-gsap-flip/) covers the grid-specific edge cases.
filterRec.a11yNotes: Respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` by skipping `Flip.getState` entirely in the click handler so the effect short-circuits and React's normal commit becomes the fallback (cards just appear in their new positions, no movement). Keep tweens under 600ms so even non-reduced-motion users aren't waiting on the filter. Tag buttons should be real `<button>` elements with `aria-pressed` reflecting the active tag, and the grid container can stay a static landmark — Flip only moves visuals, it doesn't reorder DOM source order beyond what React already does, so screen reader order follows the filtered array naturally.

inventoryNotes.notes:
EXISTING TRANSITIONS THAT WILL COLLIDE WITH GSAP — call out before wiring:

1. `.card` (NoteCard.module.css L18–22) already has `transition: transform 180ms ... , box-shadow 220ms ...`. If GSAP writes `transform` every frame on pointermove, the CSS transition will fight it — each GSAP tween will be re-eased by the CSS transition, producing a perceptible lag/smear. Two options: (a) clear the CSS transition for `transform` on the pills while the proximity effect is active (toggle a class on `.list` that sets `transition: border-color var(--transition-fast)` only on its `.collapsed` children), or (b) drive a CSS custom property (e.g. `--dock-scale`) from GSAP and let CSS apply `transform: scale(var(--dock-scale, 1))` — but the existing `:hover` rule writes `transform: translateY(-1px)` which would clobber `scale()` unless rewritten to be additive.

2. `.collapsed:hover` (L39–45) sets `transform: translateY(-1px)` and a colored `box-shadow`. With proximity hover, EVERY pill near the cursor needs the lift, not just the one being `:hover`'d. Either (a) supersede the `:hover` rule (drop the transform + shadow from `:hover`, let GSAP own them entirely and key both off proximity distance), or (b) coordinate — keep `:hover` for the focal pill and have GSAP only animate the neighbours. Cleanest is (a): the dock metaphor IS proximity, so `:hover` becomes redundant.

3. `.collapsed:active` resets transform to `translateY(0) scale(0.995)`. If GSAP owns the transform during the press, the click squish needs to be expressed as a quickTo too, or `:active` should bump CSS specificity via `!important` (last resort).

4. `.expanded` runs a 200ms `noteExpandIn` keyframe animation on swap (L106). When the user clicks a magnified pill, GSAP should release that pill's tween (reset to scale 1) BEFORE the React state swap so the keyframe animation starts from the natural transform, otherwise the expand-in will visually pop.

5. The panel itself transitions `max-height/min-height/top` over 260ms when `hasExpanded` toggles (NotesPanel.module.css L28–32, L38–45). During that 260ms, pill `getBoundingClientRect()` positions change every frame — proximity math must read live rects, not memoized ones.

6. `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` blocks (NoteCard.module.css L333–348, NotesPanel.module.css L242–252) explicitly zero the hover transform/shadow. The GSAP effect must mirror this: bail out of the listener install if reduced-motion is requested, and respond to `matchMedia` change events (writer can toggle this OS-level mid-session).

7. The pill stack is `flex-direction: column` (vertical), so this is a *vertical* proximity dock. Real macOS dock is horizontal. If the user wants horizontal magnification, the `.list` flex direction needs flipping (which conflicts with `overflow-y` scroll behavior) — worth surfacing as a clarification before building.

Recommendation: have GSAP own `scale` (+ optional `y`) and `box-shadow` via JS-set inline styles, REMOVE the existing `.collapsed:hover` `transform`/`box-shadow` rules so there's a single source of truth, keep CSS for `border-color` on hover (cheap, doesn't fight transform), and gate the whole thing behind a reduced-motion check + `expandedId == null` check.

inventoryShare.notes:
On whether to also replace the popover pop-in (CSS `@keyframes quoteShareIn`) with a GSAP entrance:

Recommendation: leave the keyframe alone in this change, OR replace it cleanly — do not stack both.

Reasons to leave it as-is
- It's brand new (PR #181), short (140ms), and tied to mount; CSS keyframes are the right tool for one-shot enter animations that don't need imperative control. The site uses CSS animations elsewhere for similar enter flashes (e.g. `.fragmentFlash` in the same file).
- Mixing a CSS `animation` on `.popover` with a GSAP tween on the same element (or its descendants) at mount risks transform-origin / will-change conflicts and clobbered transforms when GSAP also targets `transform: scale()` on buttons.
- The user asked specifically for click feedback on the share affordance — the popover entrance is a separate concern.

Reasons to convert (only if doing it)
- GSAP would give you `prefersReducedMotion()` short-circuiting in one place rather than relying on the browser's CSS-level reduced-motion handling (the current keyframe doesn't honor it — worth checking).
- An imperative `useGSAP` entrance lets the popover also play an exit tween before unmount (currently it just disappears), which is the bigger UX win than the entrance itself.
- It would unify motion idioms across the codebase — every other animated component (CardGrid, ReadingView, ExpandableSection, SiteHeader, BlockedTagsButton, ReadingPrefs, LikeButton, admin layout) already uses `useGSAP`.

If the choice is to convert: delete `animation: quoteShareIn ...` + the `@keyframes quoteShareIn` block from QuoteShare.module.css, add a `useGSAP(() => { gsap.from(popoverRef.current, { opacity: 0, y: 2, scale: 0.98, duration: 0.14, ease: 'power2.out' }) }, { scope: popoverRef, dependencies: [selection?.rect] })` so it re-plays each time a new selection mounts the popover. Then to add the exit animation, refactor mount/unmount to keep the element rendered behind an `isOpen` boolean and tween `opacity/y/scale` back to the from-state before clearing `selection`.

My suggestion for this task: ship the GSAP click pulse on both components first (small, isolated, matches LikeButton). If desired, follow up with a dedicated PR that converts the popover entrance to GSAP and adds an exit tween at the same time — that's a more substantive UX change and should not be hidden inside a 'click feedback' commit.

- ShareButton appears in three pages: app/chapter/[id]/page.tsx (line 225), app/story/[id]/page.tsx (line 174), app/series/[id]/page.tsx (line 158). The change is local to the component — no caller updates needed.

inventoryScrollRestore.currentBehavior: "Current restore is INSTANT, not animated. Sequence: (1) on mount/contentId/pageNumber change, useReadingPosition fetches the stored row; (2) if the page matches and percentage >= 4, it schedules `restore` via `requestIdleCallback(..., { timeout: 500 })` (single rAF fallback on Safari); (3) `restore()` computes `target = (pct/100) * (scrollHeight - innerHeight)` and calls `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })`. There is no tween, no easing, no GSAP involvement — `behavior: 'instant'` is the explicit choice. The reader jumps. Restore is also page-aware (paged mode only) and is silently skipped on network failure, percentage < 4, or page mismatch. Concurrent reader writes are throttled at 5s with a trailing flush and a final beacon on visibilitychange/pagehide/unmount."
inventoryScrollRestore.integrationPoints:
"Single insertion point: replace the `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` call inside the `restore` closure in lib/useReadingPosition.ts (~line 119) with a GSAP tween:

  gsap.to(window, {
    duration: 1.1, // or scale by distance: gsap.utils.clamp(0.6, 1.6, target / 1800)
    scrollTo: { y: target, autoKill: true }, // autoKill aborts if the user scrolls/wheels mid-tween
    ease: 'power2.out',
    overwrite: 'auto',
  });

Prereq edits (do these first):
  1. lib/gsap.ts — import and register ScrollToPlugin alongside ScrollTrigger inside the `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard, and re-export it. The plugin file already exists at node_modules/gsap/ScrollToPlugin.js. Without this, the tween silently no-ops.
  2. lib/useReadingPosition.ts — import `{ gsap, prefersReducedMotion }` from '@/lib/gsap'; keep the existing rIC/rAF deferral and the `target <= 0` / `!Number.isFinite(target)` guards. If `prefersReducedMotion()` returns true, fall back to the current instant `window.scrollTo`. Consider also bailing to instant when `target > scrollHeight - innerHeight` after content shift (clamp via `gsap.utils.clamp(0, doc.scrollHeight - window.innerHeight, target)`).
  3. Keep the existing rIC/rAF wrapper — it's what gets us past hydration so `scrollHeight` is real. Tweening before that point would tween to 0.

Do NOT extend TextFragmentScroller. Reasons:
  - It runs only when the URL hash contains `:~:text=`, so 100% of normal returning-reader sessions would bypass it.
  - It owns a different concern (DOM text walk + Range + block flash) on a different gating signal (hash) with a different target unit (an element, not a Y offset).
  - The two paths can co-occur on a single visit (returning reader who arrived via a shared `#:~:text=` link). The right precedence is: text-fragment wins — it represents an explicit user intent (the share link) over a stored heuristic. Make ScrollRestore defer when `window.location.hash.includes(':~:text=')` OR when `document.fragmentDirective` is going to act. Simplest implementation: inside useReadingPosition's restore() add an early `if (window.location.hash.includes(':~:text=')) return;` so the polyfill's smooth scrollIntoView (or Chromium's native one) runs unopposed. TextFragmentScroller already uses double rAF (post-hydration), useReadingPosition uses rIC; with the early bail there is no race.

Do NOT factor this into a separate ScrollRestore React component. The trigger lives entirely inside useReadingPosition's existing fetch-then-restore flow — a new component would just re-do the API call or need a prop bridge. Keep it as a one-line swap inside the hook.

Other call sites to leave alone: ReadingView's `goToPage` and `switchToPaged` use `behavior: 'auto'` deliberately (page change = jump to top); the scroll-to-top button uses native smooth scroll. Animating those via GSAP is out of scope for this task."
inventoryScrollRestore.notes: "Edge cases worth handling in the swap: (1) if the reader has already manually scrolled before rIC fires (e.g. fast-paint Safari + impatient user), `autoKill: true` plus `overwrite: 'auto'` lets us tween without yanking them — but you may also want a `Math.abs(window.scrollY - 0) > 50 ? bail : tween` guard before kicking off; (2) mode toggle: useReadingPosition is intentionally `enabled: false` in infinite mode, so the tween only runs in paged mode — matches today's behavior; (3) `restore()` closes over `cancelled`; the unmount cleanup sets it true. With a 1.1s tween in flight, kill it explicitly via `const tween = gsap.to(window, {...}); ` and call `tween.kill()` in the cleanup so a route-change during the animation doesn't keep scrolling the next page; (4) the existing `?page=N` handling in ReadingView means the hook re-fires after a page swap — make sure the tween from a stale page is killed before the new one kicks off (overwrite:'auto' covers this for back-to-back tweens on the same target)."

inventoryTagFilter.currentBehavior: "Filtering is server-driven via URL params. TagBar is a 'use client' component but it only renders next/link <Link> elements — every pill href is built by buildTagHref(id), which writes ?search=…&tagIds=<id> against basePath (default /search), and the 'All' pill href clears tagIds. There is no client filter state and no router.push: clicking a tag is a Next.js App Router navigation. SearchPage and TagPage are async Server Components that read searchParams (or the route slug), call getStories / getSeriesList with the new tagIds, and render the next CardGrid tree. The result cards (StoryCard / SeriesCard inside <CardGrid>) are wholly re-rendered each navigation — they're brand-new DOM nodes with new React keys (story.id / series.id). CardGrid's only animation today is a one-shot GSAP scrollTrigger fade-up stagger that fires once on mount (`once: true`), so subsequent filter changes don't animate the cards at all. The only places filter toggles ARE client-side and could host Flip cheaply: (1) BlockedTagsButton — useMemo sortedTags reorders the in-panel <ul> when blocked toggles or filter text changes, all in the same component tree; (2) TagPicker in admin — useMemo {selected, results} similarly reorders pills when toggle() flips a value or query changes. TagBar's own active-pill restyle does not reorder pills (sortedTags is purely alphabetical, independent of activeSet)."
inventoryTagFilter.integrationPoints: "For the primary tag-filter reorder (browse/search/tag): every filter click triggers an App Router server navigation, so the cards being reordered come from different React renders / different DOM nodes. Hook points where a FLIP-style transition could be wired in: (1) TagBar.tsx — replace the next/link <Link> on each Pill with a router.push using useRouter + useSearchParams, then drive the reorder client-side OR keep <Link> and intercept onClick with e.preventDefault before the navigation to record First positions; pair with a useGSAP/useLayoutEffect on CardGrid keyed by serialised tagIds to read Last positions and tween the deltas. (2) CardGrid.tsx — already wraps the card list and has containerRef + useGSAP; this is the natural home for the FLIP read/play loop, and it would need stable card identity exposed (e.g., data-flip-id={story.id || series.id} on StoryCard / SeriesCard root) so the same id can be matched across renders. (3) The two server pages (app/search/page.tsx, app/tag/[slug]/page.tsx) currently pass children directly into <CardGrid>; no API contract change required as long as the cards expose a stable id attribute. (4) For BlockedTagsButton + admin TagPicker the reorder is fully client-side inside one component — Flip can be wired in directly around the useMemo sort with no routing involved. (5) SearchBar at components/SearchBar.tsx already does a router.push, confirming useRouter is the established pattern for query-string updates."
inventoryTagFilter.notes: "Yes — server-driven filtering is the central blocker for a vanilla GSAP Flip plugin integration on TagBar/browse/search/tag pages. Flip's contract is read-Before -> mutate-DOM -> read-After -> animate-delta on the SAME DOM nodes (or, with Flip.fit / data-flip-id, on nodes that survived a React reconcile in place). A Next.js App Router navigation re-renders the server tree, swaps the entire <CardGrid> subtree for a fresh React mount, and discards the previous DOM nodes before Flip could ever read 'After'. Three viable workarounds, ordered by intrusiveness: (1) Lightest — let Next.js fetch but intercept the render: in TagBar replace the <Link> with router.push + Flip.getState(cards) called synchronously BEFORE push, then in CardGrid run a useLayoutEffect keyed on the searchParams tagIds (or a serialised version) that calls Flip.from(savedState, …) after the new server render mounts. React preserves DOM nodes that share the same key across renders, so as long as StoryCard/SeriesCard expose data-flip-id={id} and the parent grid is the same DOM container, GSAP can match the surviving ids and animate their position deltas; cards that appeared/disappeared get Flip's onEnter/onLeave handlers. The 'savedState' has to live somewhere that survives the navigation — a module-level Map keyed by a session-scoped token, sessionStorage, or a React context that the new server render's first useLayoutEffect drains. (2) Move filtering client-side: convert SearchPage from a Server Component to a small server shell that fetches a superset of cards once and a client component that filters locally on tagIds in URL or local state. Flip then runs in a single component with all DOM intact. Drops SSR result counts and breaks the /tag/[slug] SEO landing pages — significant. (3) Hybrid: keep server filtering for deep links / SEO but optimistically perform the new filter client-side from a cached over-fetched dataset, then reconcile with the server payload on arrival. Most work, smoothest UX. For the two purely client-side filter surfaces — BlockedTagsButton's tag list and admin TagPicker — Flip drops in cleanly with no routing surgery: wrap the useMemo sort with Flip.getState before the state change and Flip.from after, keyed on tag.id. Those are good prototypes before committing to option (1) for the main browse path. Also worth noting: CardGrid's current GSAP stagger uses `once: true`, so it would need to be guarded to not fight a Flip tween on re-render."

## Goal
Give every public-site card row and the admin notes pill list a macOS-dock proximity hover so cards near the cursor scale and lift smoothly, mirroring the canonical GSAP demo (https://demos.gsap.com/demo/macos-dock-effect/).

## Files
- New: `frontend/lib/useDockProximity.ts`
- Edit: `frontend/components/ExpandableSection.tsx`, `frontend/components/CardGrid.tsx`, `frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.tsx`, `frontend/components/ResumeReadingRow.tsx`
- Edit: `frontend/components/StoryCard.module.css`, `frontend/components/ContinueCard.module.css`, `frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.module.css` (remove CSS `:hover` transforms; keep border/box-shadow)
- Edit: `frontend/app/page.tsx` + `frontend/app/page.module.css` (extract a tiny `'use client'` wrapper around the homepage hero `.heroCardsList`)
- Edit: `frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.tsx` (add `listRef`, attach hook, skip when `expandedId != null`)
- Edit: `frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.tsx` (spread `data-dock-item` on the collapsed `.card` div)
- Edit: `frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.module.css` (drop `.collapsed:hover { transform: translateY(-1px) }` so GSAP owns transform)

## Approach
1. Implement a shared `useDockProximity(containerRef, opts)` hook using `useGSAP` from `@/lib/gsap`: enumerates `[data-dock-item]` children, builds `gsap.quickTo(child, 'scale')` + `gsap.quickTo(child, 'y')` setters per child, attaches one `pointermove` and `pointerleave` to the container, falloff `t = max(0, 1 - dist/radius)`, target `scale = 1 + t * (MAX_SCALE - 1)` and `y = -t * MAX_LIFT`.
2. Gate the listener install on `matchMedia('(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)').matches` and bail entirely when `prefersReducedMotion()` is true.
3. Re-measure with `ResizeObserver` on the container and on `deps` (e.g. children count, `notes.length`).
4. Apply to ExpandableSection, CardGrid, ContinueReadingRow (add `listRef`), ResumeReadingRow (add `listRef`), homepage hero (new client wrapper), and admin NotesPanel `.list` (axis: 'y', also gated on `expandedId == null`).
5. Tag card roots with `data-dock-item` and remove the colliding CSS `:hover { transform: ... }` rules so transform has one writer (GSAP).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Hover anywhere across `/`, `/browse`, `/search`, `/tag/[slug]`, `/story/[id]`, `/chapter/[id]`, `/series/[id]` shows smooth proximity magnification on the surrounding cards.
- [ ] Admin notes list pills magnify around the cursor; expanding a note disables the effect (only one pill in the rail).
- [ ] CSS `:hover` transform on affected card classes is removed; CSS color/border hover still works.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` users see no proximity scaling.
- [ ] Touch / coarse-pointer users see no effect (matchMedia `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`).
- [ ] Keyboard `:focus-visible` gives a visible parity state (scale equivalent or border highlight) so tab navigation isn't worse than before.
- [ ] No regression to the existing scroll-reveal stagger in CardGrid / ExpandableSection.

## Reduced motion
`useDockProximity` checks `prefersReducedMotion()` from `@/lib/gsap` on mount and on `matchMedia` change events; when true it skips installing the listeners entirely and the card row stays at its CSS resting state.
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: Hook checks `prefersReducedMotion()` from `@/lib/gsap` on mount AND subscribes to the matchMedia change event; when reduced motion is active it returns early without installing listeners or building setters, so the row keeps its un-animated CSS resting state.

tasks.title: Animate auto-height when expanding an admin note
tasks.useCase: When the user clicks a collapsed note pill in the admin NotesPanel, the panel smoothly grows from its current height to the natural height of the expanded card instead of snapping to a CSS keyframe.
tasks.approach: Add a small `AutoHeightPanel` client component (under admin/_components) that takes `open: boolean` + children, wraps them in a `<div ref={panelRef} style={{ height: 0, overflow: 'hidden' }}>`, and uses `useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: panelRef, dependencies: [open] })` to run the canonical measure-then-tween: read `startH = getBoundingClientRect().height`, set `height: auto` to read `fullH`, then `gsap.fromTo(el, { height: startH }, { height: open ? fullH : 0, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power2.inOut', onComplete: () => { if (open) gsap.set(el, { height: 'auto', overflow: '' }) } })`. In `NoteCard.tsx` the expanded body (currently rendered conditionally inside the expanded branch with a `noteExpandIn` keyframe) is wrapped in `<AutoHeightPanel open={expanded}>...</AutoHeightPanel>` so the React tree always renders both branches, with the panel collapsing to 0px when not expanded. Remove the `animation: noteExpandIn 200ms` rule from `NoteCard.module.css` so GSAP owns the entrance; keep the swap-in opacity fade as a tiny child tween started in `onStart`. Reduced-motion path: when `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, the hook skips the tween and just `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })` synchronously. Cleanup is automatic via `useGSAP` revert on unmount; `overflow: hidden` is removed on complete so focus rings and dropdown menus inside the expanded note are not clipped.
risks: The current `noteExpandIn` keyframe and the panel's existing 260ms max-height transition on `.panel` (hasExpanded toggle) could double-animate — the panel-level transition must stay (it grows the aside), and only the per-note body grows via GSAP.

Re-measuring on every `open` change is correct, but if the note's content changes while open (e.g. typing), height freezes at `auto` so it grows naturally — verify this works inside the existing contenteditable / textarea.
Color picker / 3-dot menu popovers inside the note must not be clipped — ensure `overflow: ''` is restored on complete and never re-applied while open.
Focus management: when collapsing a note that contains a focused textarea, focus should be moved out before the height tween so it doesn't land in a 0-height region.

## Goal
Make the admin note expansion grow smoothly from collapsed pill to fully expanded card using GSAP's canonical animate-to-height-auto pattern, replacing the current 200ms `noteExpandIn` CSS keyframe.

## Files
- New: `frontend/app/admin/_components/AutoHeightPanel.tsx`
- Edit: `frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.tsx` (wrap the expanded body with `<AutoHeightPanel open={expanded}>`)
- Edit: `frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.module.css` (remove `animation: noteExpandIn ...`)
- Edit: `frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.tsx` (only if needed to reconcile the panel-level `hasExpanded` transition with the new tween)

## Approach
1. Build `AutoHeightPanel` as a `'use client'` component using `useGSAP` from `@/lib/gsap` with `dependencies: [open]`.
2. On every `open` flip: snapshot `startH`, force `height: auto` to read `fullH`, `gsap.fromTo(el, { height: startH }, { height: open ? fullH : 0, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power2.inOut', overflow: 'hidden' })`.
3. `onComplete`: when `open === true`, restore `height: 'auto'` and clear `overflow` so the panel reflows naturally and inner popovers are not clipped.
4. Wrap the expanded NoteCard body inside `<AutoHeightPanel open={expanded}>` so both branches render and React only toggles the boolean.
5. Drop the CSS `noteExpandIn` keyframe; keep the panel-level (.panel) max-height transition for the aside frame.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Clicking a collapsed pill smoothly grows the card to its natural content height (no pop, no snap).
- [ ] Collapsing tweens back to 0 over the same duration.
- [ ] After expansion completes, `height` is `auto` and `overflow` is unset so typing into the note (or opening the color picker) reflows naturally and is not clipped.
- [ ] Reduced-motion users get an instant height set, no animation.
- [ ] No conflict with the existing aside-level `hasExpanded` max-height transition.

## Reduced motion
`AutoHeightPanel` checks `prefersReducedMotion()` from `@/lib/gsap` inside the `useGSAP` callback and replaces the tween with `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })`, so the panel toggles instantly with no animation.
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: `AutoHeightPanel` checks `prefersReducedMotion()` at the start of the `useGSAP` callback and substitutes a synchronous `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })` instead of the fromTo tween.

tasks.title: Add GSAP click feedback to Like / Save / Share with per-button color flash
tasks.useCase: When a reader clicks LIKE, SAVE, or SHARE in the reading footer, the pill plays a short, tactile scale+color-flash so the action feels acknowledged even before the network round-trip completes.
tasks.gsapPlugin: gsap core (timeline with elastic.out + back.out + CSS variable tween)
tasks.demoReference: https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/RwMQwpR (canonical `gsap.matchMedia` reduced-motion gate) + https://github.com/greensock/react#contextsafe (useGSAP + contextSafe click handler pattern)
tasks.approach: Define a tiny shared helper `pulseButton(el, color)` (inline in each component, or factored into `frontend/lib/buttonPulse.ts` if all three end up identical) that builds a `gsap.timeline({ defaults: { overwrite: 'auto' } })` of: `.to(el, { scale: 0.88, duration: 0.08, ease: 'power2.out' })` then `.to(el, { scale: 1, duration: 0.42, ease: 'back.out(2.4)' })`, plus a parallel `.fromTo(el, { '--pulse-flash': 0 }, { '--pulse-flash': 1, duration: 0.18, ease: 'power1.out' }, 0).to(el, { '--pulse-flash': 0, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power1.in' }, 0.18)`. Each button's CSS module gets a `box-shadow: 0 0 0 calc(var(--pulse-flash, 0) * 6px) color-mix(in oklab, transparent, var(--button-color) calc(var(--pulse-flash, 0) * 60%))` so the color flash is a per-button glow keyed off a CSS variable — `--button-color` is `--like` on LikeButton, `--gold` on SaveButton, and `--gold-soft` (or `--text-muted`) on ShareButton (final palette per the open question). LikeButton already has the ref + useGSAP scope; SaveButton needs `useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)`, `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })`, and the `contextSafe`-wrapped `pulse()` call at the top of `toggle()` (skipping the anonymous Link variant entirely). ShareButton gets the same treatment, called at the top of `onShare`. QuoteShare wires a one-shot `gsap.fromTo(e.currentTarget, { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.12, yoyo: true, repeat: 1, duration: 0.1, ease: 'power2.out' })` from inside `onShareClick(target, i, e)` — color flash optional there since the existing `.buttonCopied` gold flash already covers confirmation. CSS variable tweening through `gsap.to(el, { '--pulse-flash': 1 })` requires that the variable exist as a registered custom property OR be referenced in a style declaration on the element — using it inside `box-shadow` keeps it live without needing `@property`.
SaveButton anonymous variant is an `<a>` Link — must NOT attach the pulse there.

ShareButton sits in the same row as Like/Save and uses neutral colors; if the flash color isn't tied to a real `--share` token, choose a neutral (`--text-muted` or `--gold-soft`) to avoid implying a 'success' meaning.
QuoteShare's brand buttons (X/Facebook/Bluesky) call `dismiss()` immediately after `window.open`, killing the popover and the in-flight tween — that's fine but be aware the visual is truncated.

## Goal
Replace LikeButton's existing simple scale pulse and add equivalent (per-button color-themed) click feedback to SaveButton, ShareButton, and QuoteShare's toolbar buttons so the reading-footer action row reads with a single consistent motion language.

## Files
- Edit: `frontend/components/LikeButton.tsx` + `frontend/components/LikeButton.module.css`
- Edit: `frontend/components/SaveButton.tsx` + `frontend/components/SaveButton.module.css`
- Edit: `frontend/components/ShareButton.tsx` + `frontend/components/ShareButton.module.css`
- Edit: `frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx`
- Optional: `frontend/lib/buttonPulse.ts` if the helper is factored out

## Approach
1. Build a `pulse(el, colorVar)` helper that runs a 3-step timeline: scale 1 → 0.88 (80ms power2.out) → 1 (420ms back.out(2.4)), with a parallel `--pulse-flash` 0→1→0 tween (~430ms total).
2. Each CSS module declares `box-shadow: 0 0 0 calc(var(--pulse-flash, 0) * 6px) color-mix(in oklab, transparent, var(--button-color) calc(var(--pulse-flash, 0) * 60%))` and sets `--button-color` per component (`--like` / `--gold` / `--gold-soft`).
3. Wire into each component via `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })` + `contextSafe(() => pulse(...))`, called at the top of the existing onClick handler.
4. Skip the pulse when `prefersReducedMotion()` is true (state still toggles).
5. Skip entirely on the anonymous SaveButton `<a>` variant.
6. In QuoteShare, run a one-shot `gsap.fromTo(e.currentTarget, ...)` inside `onShareClick(target, i, e)`; do not touch the popover's existing entrance keyframe in this PR.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Clicking Like / Save / Share plays the same length/feel scale pulse with a per-button color flash glow.
- [ ] The flash color matches the button's active-state token (`--like` for Like, `--gold` for Save, agreed token for Share — see open question).
- [ ] Spam clicks restart the animation cleanly (no queued or stacked tweens).
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` users see no animation but the toggle state still flips.
- [ ] SaveButton anonymous Link variant has no animation hook (still a plain navigation).
- [ ] QuoteShare toolbar buttons get the scale pulse on click; copy buttons still show the existing `.buttonCopied` gold confirmation.

## Reduced motion
Each `pulse()` call is wrapped in `if (prefersReducedMotion()) return;` from `@/lib/gsap`, after the optimistic state mutation, so reduced-motion users still see the state change but no scale or flash animation.
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: `pulse()` short-circuits when `prefersReducedMotion()` returns true; the optimistic state still flips and aria-pressed updates so the action remains fully usable, just without motion.

tasks.title: Tween scroll restore back to last reading position with ScrollToPlugin
tasks.useCase: When a returning reader opens a story or chapter they were partway through, the page smoothly animates the window down to their saved scroll offset instead of snapping with `behavior: 'instant'`.
tasks.approach: Register ScrollToPlugin in `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` alongside ScrollTrigger inside the existing `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard and re-export it. In `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts`, swap the single `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` call inside `restore()` for a `gsap.to(window, { duration: 1.1, scrollTo: { y: Math.min(target, doc.scrollHeight - innerHeight), autoKill: true, onAutoKill: () => { /* no-op */ } }, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' })`, keeping the existing `requestIdleCallback`/rAF deferral and the `>= RESTORE_MIN_PERCENT` gate. Add three early bails before the tween: (a) if `prefersReducedMotion()` from `@/lib/gsap` is true, fall back to the existing `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })`; (b) if `window.location.hash.includes(':~:text=')` OR `window.location.hash.length > 1`, skip entirely so `TextFragmentScroller` (or native Chromium fragment directive) owns the arrival; (c) if `Math.abs(window.scrollY) > 50` (user has already scrolled before rIC fired), skip. Capture the tween in a local `tween` variable and call `tween.kill()` in the existing `cancelled`/cleanup path so a route-change mid-tween does not keep scrolling the next page. Do not extend `TextFragmentScroller`; do not refactor into a separate component.
risks: Document height can shift after hydration (font load, image swap, async RichText) — `target` may exceed scrollMax; clamp via `Math.min(target, doc.scrollHeight - innerHeight)` to avoid landing short.

If `html { scroll-behavior: smooth }` is ever set globally it will fight ScrollToPlugin and break `autoKill` — verify globals.css has none, and add a comment in `lib/gsap.ts` warning future contributors.
Chrome trackpad `wheel` autoKill historically under-fires — may need a belt-and-braces `wheel`/`touchstart` listener calling `gsap.killTweensOf(window)` as backup.
Page-change (paged-mode `goToPage`) currently uses `behavior: 'auto'` — leave that alone; only the saved-position restore is in scope.
Hash precedence: a deep-link to `#:~:text=...` from a shared quote MUST win over the stored heuristic restore — handled by the early bail.

## Goal
Upgrade the existing reading-position restore from `behavior: 'instant'` to a 1.1s GSAP ScrollToPlugin tween so returning readers smoothly travel back to where they left off, without breaking deep-link text-fragments or trapping users who start scrolling mid-animation.

## Files
- Edit: `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` (register and re-export ScrollToPlugin)
- Edit: `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts` (swap the `restore()` call site)

## Approach
1. In `lib/gsap.ts`, add `import { ScrollToPlugin } from 'gsap/ScrollToPlugin';` and `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, ScrollToPlugin);` inside the existing `typeof window !== 'undefined'` block. Re-export it.
2. In `useReadingPosition.ts`, inside `restore()` (keep the existing `requestIdleCallback` deferral and `>= RESTORE_MIN_PERCENT` gate), early-bail when: `prefersReducedMotion()` (fall back to instant `window.scrollTo`), `window.location.hash` contains `:~:text=` or any other anchor (let `TextFragmentScroller` / native fragment directive win), or `window.scrollY > 50` (user already moved).
3. Replace the `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` call with `const tween = gsap.to(window, { duration: 1.1, scrollTo: { y: Math.min(target, doc.scrollHeight - innerHeight), autoKill: true }, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' });` and store `tween` for cleanup.
4. Extend the existing `cancelled` cleanup path to call `tween?.kill()` so route-changes mid-tween don't carry scroll into the next page.
5. Do NOT change `TextFragmentScroller`, `ReadingView.goToPage`, or the scroll-to-top button.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Returning to a story/chapter with a saved position >= 4% smoothly tweens to that offset over ~1.1s.
- [ ] Arriving with a `#:~:text=...` URL skips the tween entirely (TextFragmentScroller / native fragment directive runs unopposed).
- [ ] Wheel/touch/scrollbar input during the tween cancels it (`autoKill: true`).
- [ ] Reduced-motion users get the existing instant restore behavior.
- [ ] Navigating away mid-tween does not carry scroll onto the next page.
- [ ] Page-mode swaps and the scroll-to-top button still use their existing native scroll (not regressed).

## Reduced motion
`restore()` checks `prefersReducedMotion()` and falls back to the original `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` instead of constructing the GSAP tween, so reduced-motion users land at the saved position with zero animation.

tasks.approach: Register `Flip` in `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` and re-export. For the public browse/search/tag surfaces — server-driven filtering is the load-bearing constraint, so use the lightest of the three workarounds in the inventory: `TagBar` keeps `<Link>` but intercepts the click with `e.preventDefault()`, synchronously calls `Flip.getState('[data-flip-id]', { props: 'opacity' })`, stores the state in a module-level Map (`frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts`) keyed by a session-scoped token derived from the new path+query, then `router.push(href)`. After the server navigation commits, `CardGrid`'s `useGSAP` (keyed on serialised `tagIds` from `useSearchParams`) drains the stored state and runs `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.55, ease: 'power2.inOut', absolute: true, stagger: 0.02, onEnter: el => gsap.fromTo(el, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92 }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.35 }), onLeave: el => gsap.to(el, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, duration: 0.25 }) })`. Cards expose `data-flip-id={story.id || series.id}` on their root so the matcher survives a React re-mount. The bridge clears itself after `Flip.from` completes and on a timeout fallback (so a back-navigation doesn't apply stale state to a different route). For the two purely client-side surfaces — `BlockedTagsButton` and admin `TagPicker` — drop Flip in directly around the existing `useMemo` sort: capture before the toggle setState in the click handler, run `Flip.from` in a `useLayoutEffect` keyed on the order signature. Reduced-motion: skip `Flip.getState` entirely so the bridge stores nothing and the next render just commits without animation. CardGrid's existing scroll-reveal stagger (`once: true`) is guarded to not re-run after the first mount, so it won't fight the Flip tween — but add an `overwrite: 'auto'` on the Flip tween for safety.
risks: Server-side filtering means new DOM nodes — the bridge approach relies on Flip's `data-flip-id` matching surviving cards across a route change; if React's reconciler can't preserve the grid container between server renders, only `onEnter` will fire (degraded but not broken).

Module-level state survives route changes but also survives them too well — must clear after Flip.from completes AND on a setTimeout fallback (1.5s) so a back-button or fast tag-toggle doesn't apply stale 'before' positions to a different result set.

App Router prefetch + cache may make the navigation feel near-instant; need to verify that `useGSAP` keyed on `useSearchParams` actually re-runs after the server navigation (not just on the first render).

`absolute: true` briefly pulls cards out of flow during the tween — the CardGrid container must have a stable height during the tween or items below will jump; may need `Flip.from(state, { absolute: true, simple: true })` with a held min-height during animation.

If the grid is wrapped in `<Suspense>` with streaming, the cards may mount in batches — Flip would only see the first batch's positions; verify with the actual streaming behavior or fall back to capturing onComplete from the navigation event.

Tags can ALSO be filtered by navigating to `/tag/[slug]` — that's a different route entirely and the Flip bridge won't span it; scope this PR to TagBar-driven reorders within /search and document /tag/[slug] as out of scope.
BlockedTagsButton and TagPicker are unaffected by the routing complexity — they should land first as a proof-of-concept before the browse path.

## Goal
Replace the current snap re-render after a TagBar click with a GSAP Flip tween that animates surviving cards from their old grid positions to their new positions, with fade-scale enter/leave for cards filtered in/out.

## Files
- New: `frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts` (module-level Map for handing Flip state across a server navigation)
- Edit: `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` (register + re-export Flip)
- Edit: `frontend/components/TagBar.tsx` (intercept click, capture Flip state, then `router.push`)
- Edit: `frontend/components/CardGrid.tsx` (drain Flip state in `useGSAP` keyed on `useSearchParams.toString()`)
- Edit: `frontend/components/StoryCard.tsx` + `frontend/components/SeriesCard.tsx` (add `data-flip-id={id}` to root)
- Edit: `frontend/components/BlockedTagsButton.tsx` (in-panel Flip on sortedTags reorder)
- Edit: `frontend/app/admin/_components/TagPicker.tsx` (Flip on selected/results reorder)

## Approach
1. Register Flip in `lib/gsap.ts`.
2. Build `flipBridge` as a module-level `Map<string, Flip.FlipState>` keyed by a path+query token, with a `setState(token, state)` / `consumeState(token): Flip.FlipState | null` API and a 1.5s expiry timer.
3. In TagBar's Pill onClick: `e.preventDefault()`, derive the next token, capture `Flip.getState('[data-flip-id]', { props: 'opacity' })`, stash it in the bridge, then `router.push(href)`.
4. In CardGrid: `useGSAP(() => { const state = flipBridge.consumeState(currentToken); if (!state) return; Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.55, ease: 'power2.inOut', absolute: true, stagger: 0.02, onEnter, onLeave, overwrite: 'auto' }) }, { dependencies: [searchParams.toString()] })`.
5. Cards expose `data-flip-id={id}` on their outer wrapper.
6. BlockedTagsButton + TagPicker: capture in the click handler before setState; run `Flip.from` in a `useLayoutEffect` keyed on the resulting order signature.
7. Reduced-motion: skip `Flip.getState` in the click handler so the bridge stays empty and the render commits without animation.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Toggling a tag in TagBar on `/search` smoothly moves surviving cards from their old grid positions to their new ones (no snap).
- [ ] Cards filtered in fade-scale up; cards filtered out fade-scale down.
- [ ] BlockedTagsButton's in-panel sort reorder animates smoothly when toggling blocked or typing in the search box.
- [ ] Admin TagPicker's selected/unselected pill split animates smoothly when toggling a tag.
- [ ] Reduced-motion users see the original snap behavior.
- [ ] No regression to CardGrid's first-mount scroll-reveal stagger.
- [ ] `/tag/[slug]` route changes do NOT carry a Flip animation (explicitly out of scope) — bridge expires safely.

## Reduced motion
In TagBar's onClick, the call to `Flip.getState` is wrapped in `if (!prefersReducedMotion()) { ... }` so the bridge is never populated; CardGrid's `useGSAP` then has nothing to consume and the new server render commits with no animation.
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: TagBar's click handler wraps the `Flip.getState` capture in `if (!prefersReducedMotion()) { ... }`, so under reduced motion the bridge stays empty and CardGrid's `useGSAP` short-circuits to render-with-no-animation (the existing snap behavior).

Admin-only surface, smallest visual footprint, and the `AutoHeightPanel` component is reusable — landing it before T1 means T1's NotesPanel work can compose with it cleanly (an expanded note inside the dock-list still needs to grow smoothly).

Public-site visual change touching many files; sequencing it after T2 lets the admin notes integration benefit from the AutoHeightPanel already being in place. The shared `useDockProximity` hook is also the first piece of GSAP infrastructure that needs `data-*` attributes on card roots — useful precedent for T5's `data-flip-id`.

Highest-risk and biggest unknown (server-driven routing vs Flip's in-place DOM contract). Saving it for last lets us ship the two purely client-side Flip surfaces (BlockedTagsButton, TagPicker) as a small first PR to prove the integration, then tackle the server-routing flipBridge in a second PR with all other GSAP infrastructure already battle-tested.

The plan uses a module-level `flipBridge` Map keyed by a path+query token to hand Flip state across the navigation — this is the lightest workaround but depends on React's reconciler preserving the CardGrid container across server renders. Are you OK with this risk profile, or would you rather (a) convert /search and /tag to client-side filtering (loses SSR result counts, breaks /tag/[slug] SEO landing), or (b) hybrid (over-fetch + client filter + reconcile, most work, smoothest UX)? T4: When a returning reader arrives via a `#:~:text=...` shared quote URL, who should win — the saved-position restore, or the text-fragment scroll? Plan defaults to text-fragment wins (skip the restore tween entirely if any hash is present). Confirm or override.
T4: Tween duration of 1.1s with `power2.out` and `autoKill: true` is the default; do you want a distance-aware duration (longer trips take ~1.6s, short ~0.6s) or a fixed 1.1s for everyone?

T3: What `--button-color` should ShareButton flash use? Plan candidates: `--gold-soft` (matches the existing Save token family, reads as a neutral confirmation) or `--text-muted` (most neutral, no implicit success meaning) or introduce a new `--share` token. LikeButton = `--like`, SaveButton = `--gold` are unambiguous; ShareButton is the only one without a clear active-color token.

T3: Should the popover entrance in QuoteShare (currently a 140ms CSS `quoteShareIn` keyframe added in PR #181) be converted to GSAP in this same PR, or left alone and tackled as a follow-up (recommended in the inventory)?

T1: Admin NotesPanel `.list` is `flex-direction: column`, so the dock-proximity will magnify vertically (cursor Y distance), not horizontally like a real macOS dock. Is vertical magnification the desired effect, or should the layout be flipped to horizontal first (which conflicts with the panel's `overflow-y: auto` scroll)?

T1: Magnification parameters — radius 200px, max scale 1.4 (lower than the canonical 1.8 because the cards are larger than dock icons), max lift 12px. Confirm or override these tuning numbers before implementation.

'auto' : 0 })` but in the same component the GSAP path uses `overflow: 'hidden'` during tween — the reduced-motion path doesn't set overflow at all, so on the FIRST mount when collapsed, the user will see content overflow before the height collapses (no `overflow: hidden` on the 0-height collapsed state).
